scope: Owner intent before native Better Auth commands in the main React workspace; local production runtime

before.signOutTestNote: The old sign-out navigated to the guest screen; its trace confirms HTTP 200 even though the test also timed out during cleanup
before.passwordFixture: Two synthetic teachers reused the same password; no real user credentials were read or changed

implementation.client: Captured-owner SDK facade for signOut, revokeOtherSessions and changePassword; canonical session reads remain unhinted
implementation.server: Better Auth onRequest plugin after native rate limiting, using database-backed getSession with disableCookieCache and disableRefresh
implementation.mismatch: 409 SESSION_CHANGED, private/no-store, no Set-Cookie and no automatic mutation replay
implementation.missingSession: 401 except POST sign-out cleanup for an already invalidated session
implementation.lifecycle: Old workspace and security/password forms suppress post-await UI effects after unmount
implementation.confirmedDelete: Failure of secondary sign-out cleanup does not report the committed account deletion as failed; the active view reloads canonical state

verification.nativePasswordBudget: Three rejected intent attempts get 409; the fourth gets 429 and native X-Retry-After
verification.agedSession: Rejected intent preserves exact updatedAt and expiresAt, with no Set-Cookie

runtimeIncident.firstTargetedRun: One unexpected exit 139 caused an initial session transport error; root cause remains unresolved
runtimeIncident.laterRuns: No additional restart across the passing 9-case retry, 42-case Chromium suite and 12-case WebKit suite before planned email-mode recreations

limits: This is a pre-command intent fence; late Set-Cookie delivery from an already dispatched auth response still needs a separate audit
Lite and older clients without the hint still need their own owner-observation implementation
Already committed server mutations are not rolled back
The isolated native-process exit still needs investigation; successful repeats do not prove runtime stability
This native-auth change requires its own complete remote CI run; no public or paid deployment was performed
